skill.name: gh-ticket
skill.description: Create and update GitHub issues with captured context, requirements, acceptance criteria, implementation notes, and GitHub CLI guidance.
skill.summary: Create complete GitHub issue specs with context, requirements, acceptance criteria, and implementation notes.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code examples. Confirmed risks remain around shell command substitution, predictable temporary file use, remote GitHub issue mutation, and possible disclosure of sensitive context in tickets.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitution for issue bodies
remediation.suggestion: Avoid embedding generated ticket text inside shell command substitution. Prefer a reviewed body file or a GitHub API call that does not require shell parsing.
Use a unique mktemp path with restrictive permissions, delete it after use, and avoid storing sensitive issue text in shared temporary locations.

remediation.issue: Sensitive context can be published to GitHub issues
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory redaction checklist for secrets, tokens, personal data, private URLs, logs, and environment details before any gh issue command.

remediation.issue: Remote issue changes lack an explicit confirmation step
remediation.suggestion: Require the agent to show the final title, body, comments, and labels, then ask for user confirmation before creating or editing GitHub issues.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Sensitive Data Disclosure in GitHub Issues
semantic_findings.description: The skill urges users to capture maximum context, fresh error messages, config values, and environment details, then publish the ticket through GitHub commands. Without explicit redaction guidance, secrets, private logs, or internal operational details can be disclosed to GitHub issues.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly request broad context, error messages, config values, and environment details, and show commands that publish issue bodies. The risk depends on user content, but the absence of redaction safeguards makes the disclosure path clear.

semantic_findings.title: Remote GitHub Issue Mutation Without Confirmation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill provides commands to create issues, replace issue bodies, add comments, and add labels, but it does not require an explicit confirmation step before remote changes. An agent following the instructions could modify project issue state with incorrect or sensitive content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited command examples perform remote GitHub create, edit, comment, and label operations. No nearby instruction requires previewing and confirming the final remote mutation.

content.value_statement: Vague issues slow implementation and lose investigation context. This skill turns findings, requirements, and acceptance criteria into complete GitHub tickets.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation and updates for GitHub issues.
Structures context, requirements, edge cases, and acceptance criteria.
Captures affected files, code locations, dependencies, and scope boundaries.
Provides GitHub CLI examples for creating, editing, commenting, and labeling issues.
Includes bug report and feature request examples.
Recommends Mermaid diagrams for complex flows and component relationships.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access for command examples.
Does not verify issue content for secrets or private data.
Does not implement code changes or run tests by itself.
May need editing for teams with custom issue templates.

use_cases.title: Write a Bug Ticket After Investigation
use_cases.description: Capture symptoms, errors, affected files, expected behavior, and testable acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Turn a Feature Request Into a Workable Spec
use_cases.description: Convert a broad request into requirements, dependencies, implementation notes, and out-of-scope items.

use_cases.title: Update an Existing Issue With New Findings
use_cases.description: Add discovered context, revised requirements, or comments while preserving useful project history.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Ticket
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner ticket creation from a short request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub issue for this request. Include summary, context, requirements, edge cases, and acceptance criteria: [request]

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Bug Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Bug ticket after reproducing a problem.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bug ticket from these findings. Include current behavior, desired behavior, error messages, affected files, and validation steps: [findings]

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Add new investigation context to an open issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update issue #[number] with this new context. Decide whether to rewrite the body or add a comment, then prepare the final ticket text: [context]

prompt_templates.title: Create a Detailed Implementation Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a multi-file change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a comprehensive GitHub ticket for this implementation. Include dependencies, out-of-scope items, affected files, key code locations, risks, and a Mermaid diagram if useful: [details]

output_examples.input: A file upload crashes for files larger than 10MB.
output_examples.output: A bug ticket with summary, current and desired behavior, file size requirements, edge cases, acceptance checks, affected upload files, and technical notes.

output_examples.input: Users need a dark mode setting.
output_examples.output: A feature ticket with product context, theme options, persistence requirements, affected settings files, dependencies, and clear out-of-scope items.

output_examples.input: New investigation found a related pull request and a missing acceptance criterion.
output_examples.output: An issue update or comment that adds the pull request link, revised acceptance criteria, and implementation notes without losing prior context.

best_practices: Review ticket content for secrets, tokens, personal data, and internal URLs before publishing.
Use exact file paths and line numbers when they are known.
Show the final issue body and labels before creating or editing a remote issue.
anti_patterns: Creating vague tickets that only say to fix or improve something.
Publishing logs, configuration values, or stack traces without redaction.
Changing an issue scope without documenting what moved out of scope.

faq.question: Does this skill create GitHub issues automatically?
faq.answer: It provides GitHub CLI command patterns, but the user or agent must run them with repository access.

faq.question: Can it update existing issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to replace the issue body, update the title, add labels, or add a comment.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: No. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can read instructions and use local tools.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing a ticket?
faq.answer: Check that requirements are specific, acceptance criteria are testable, and sensitive data has been removed.

faq.question: Can it include diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Mermaid diagrams for flows, state changes, component relationships, and process timelines.

faq.question: What are the main security concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are shell command examples, temporary file handling, remote GitHub writes, and accidental disclosure of sensitive context.
